diagnosis: Check C2 passed in multiple rollouts (0, 1, 2) despite the decision-maker lacking access to PF1; the model defaulted to a 'safe' 24-hour quarantine and battery removal based on general safety heuristics. Similarly, C5 passed in rollout 1 without access to PF3, likely because the model defaulted to a standard 4-hour fire watch period common in industrial safety protocols.

C2.why: The internal cell-damage finding changes the battery decision from an unspecified hold to removal and exactly 24 hours of steel-cabinet isolation, and it supplies the required cited justification.

C5.why: The thermal scan changes the electrical response to a 6-hour C-12 shutdown and fixes the post-reopening fire watch at exactly 4 hours.
